Page 3
SAF1 - Junior analyst vs senior analyst responsibility
1. Why it matters
A report can be technically correct and still damage a decision. Senior-level analysis means noticing what has not
been defined, what could
make the number wrong, and what another person needs in order to trust and reuse the work.
2. What you are learning
Separate task execution from decision ownership. Build a small ownership checklist that covers the decision, metric
definition, grain/source,
validation, risk communication, and handoff.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
Course 1 basics: you can clean a small dataset, calculate a metric, and explain a chart. You do not need senior job
experience.
4. Picture it in your head
Decision guardrail: Picture a dashboard request arriving at a safety gate. A junior response asks, "Can I build
it?" A senior response checks six locks before opening the gate: decision -> definition -> grain/source ->
validation -> risk -> handoff. The software comes after the locks.
5. New words before we use them
Decision owner: The person accountable for choosing the business rule or action. Acceptance criterion: A concrete
check that tells you whether the analysis
is good enough to use. Traceability: The ability to connect a conclusion back to definitions, source data, calculations,
and decisions.
6. Watch / visual source
INTERNAL TEACHING ROUTE. No external video is required for this lesson. Use the mental model and worked
demonstration below as the canonical
teaching route.
7. Follow with me once
- Stakeholder says: 'Build the weekly sales dashboard by Friday.' A task-only response begins choosing charts.
- First ask what decision Friday's meeting must make. Assume the answer is: decide whether to change the weekend
promotion.
- Write the minimum ownership contract: decision = promotion decision; metric = net revenue and margin; period =
last 8 comparable weeks;
- grain = order line; exclusions = cancelled orders; sources = orders + returns + finance control.
- Add one acceptance criterion: net revenue must reconcile to the finance weekly control within the agreed tolerance
before recommendation.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A short decision-protection checklist. It names the decision, definition, grain/source, validation check, and unresolved
item before chart design begins.
9. Why it worked
The work is now judged by whether it supports a decision safely, not by whether a dashboard exists. Professional
upgrade: In professional teams, senior
analysts often spend more time reducing ambiguity, defining controls, documenting assumptions, and negotiating
acceptance criteria than junior analysts
expect.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 4
10. Common beginner mistakes
1. Starting with chart colours or formulas. | 2. Treating the stakeholder's wording as a complete specification. | 3.
Calling yourself 'senior' because
you used an advanced tool. | 4. Hiding an unresolved definition so the work looks finished.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Write one sentence: 'What decision could be wrong if my analysis is wrong?' Then list the definition, source, and
validation most likely to affect that
decision. If still stuck: (1) restate the decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the
workbook; (4) save your genuine
attempt before opening review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Operations asks, 'Why are refunds high? Send me something today.' Create a six-line ownership
checklist before doing any calculation.
13. Validate your result
A different analyst should be able to answer: What decision is being supported? Which metric definition is still open?
What evidence would block
delivery?
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain in 60-90 seconds why senior responsibility is not the same thing as using more advanced software.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Save your genuine attempt. Only then open the protected SAF1 review. Close it and repeat on a changed scenario
without copying wording.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Ownership checklist + one validation criterion + 60-90 second explain-back. Master only when you can reproduce the
pattern on a new request. After
saving evidence, continue to SAF2.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 5
SAF2 - Turning vague stakeholder requests into scoped
analysis
1. Why it matters
Most real requests arrive incomplete: 'sales are down', 'customers are leaving', 'make a dashboard'. If you calculate
before scoping, you can
answer the wrong question perfectly.
2. What you are learning
Convert a vague request into an analysis brief: decision, audience, deadline, period, metric, grain, segments,
exclusions, sources, and
acceptance test.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
SAF1 ownership mindset. Course 1 metric and filtering basics.
4. Picture it in your head
Scoping funnel: Start with a wide, vague sentence at the top. Narrow it through decision -> audience -> KPI ->
population/time -> grain/source -> deliverable -> acceptance. If any stage is blank, the request is still too wide
to analyze safely.
5. New words before we use them
Scope: The agreed boundary of what the analysis will and will not answer. Comparison period: The time period used
as the reference for saying something
increased or decreased. Exclusion: A record or population deliberately left out for a stated reason.
6. Watch / visual source
Scoped analysis brief + unresolved-question list + acceptance test + explain-back. RECOMMENDED VIDEO -
requirements interview 00:00-05:42: problem
definition, gathering, refinement. Use for questioning technique; the book controls the course
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iIAbSOvf96E
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report.
Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
source.
7. Follow with me once
- Do not calculate yet. Ask: 'Which decision will this analysis support?' Assume: decide whether to reduce the
September promotion.
- Define the audience and deadline: Sales Director, Monday 10:00.
- Define the metric: net revenue after returns, not gross order value. Comparison: September vs August and vs same
month last year.
- Declare grain and segments: order-line grain, region and product category. Exclude cancelled orders; keep returns
as negative adjustments.
- Choose sources and acceptance: order lines + return events; reconcile monthly net revenue to Finance before
recommendation.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A one-page analysis brief where a colleague could tell exactly what is being answered and what remains out of
scope.
9. Why it worked
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 6
Each ambiguous word was converted into a decision or measurable contract before tools were used. Professional
upgrade: A strong scope note also records
what is explicitly out of scope and what would trigger a scope change. This protects both quality and delivery time.
10. Common beginner mistakes
1. Using 'sales' without defining gross vs net. | 2. Comparing unequal time windows. | 3. Adding every possible
segment instead of the ones
relevant to the decision. | 4. Letting the deadline force silent assumptions.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Circle every vague noun or adjective in the request: sales, active, high, recent, best, churned. Replace each with a
definition or an open question. If still
stuck: (1) restate the decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the workbook; (4)
save your genuine attempt before
opening review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Product says, 'Customers are churning after onboarding. Find the problem.' Build the scoped brief;
do not calculate churn.
13. Validate your result
Someone who did not attend the request meeting must be able to restate the decision, population, time window,
metric, and exclusions from your brief.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why 'clarify before calculate' saves time even when the stakeholder says the request is urgent.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Save the independent brief first. Review only after attempt, then rebuild using a changed metric or time window.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Scoped analysis brief + unresolved-question list + acceptance test + explain-back. RECOMMENDED VIDEO -
requirements interview 00:00-05:42:
problem definition, gathering, refinement. Use for questioning technique; the book controls the course
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iIAbSOvf96E
After saving evidence, continue to SAF3.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 7
SAF3 - Requirements gathering and clarification meetings
1. Why it matters
A meeting is useful only if it changes uncertainty into recorded decisions. Beginners often ask many questions but fail
to record who
approved what, by when, and what happens if no answer arrives.
2. What you are learning
Plan a short clarification meeting, ask only analysis-changing questions, capture owners and decisions, and leave
unresolved items visible.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
SAF2 scoped analysis brief.
4. Picture it in your head
Clarification tree: Imagine a meeting as a branching tree. Every answer creates the next useful question. Follow
four branches - decision, definition, data, acceptance - and keep an "open / owner / due" log so uncertainty is
visible rather than forgotten.
5. New words before we use them
Elicitation: Drawing out information or requirements from stakeholders. Decision log: A dated record of questions,
answers, owners, and unresolved items.
Escalation: Routing an unresolved decision to the person with authority to decide it.
6. Watch / visual source
Agenda + decision log + owner map + read-back summary + explain-back. RECOMMENDED VIDEO - requirements
interview 00:50-05:42: problem definition
through refinement.
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iIAbSOvf96E
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report.
Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
source.
7. Follow with me once
- Prepare three questions only: Which revenue definition is approved? Are returns recognized on return date or
original order date? Which
- regions are in scope?
- For every question, write why the answer can change the analysis. This prevents low-value questioning.
- During the meeting, record answer + owner + date. If the owner cannot decide, record the escalation owner.
- End by reading back the decisions and open items. Ask: 'If these are correct, may I proceed with this scope?'
- Send the decision log with the analysis brief. Do not rely on memory or chat history as the only record.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A meeting agenda and decision log with questions tied to analytical impact, named owners, status, and deadline.
9. Why it worked
The meeting produced an auditable contract instead of a collection of informal comments. Professional upgrade: In
high-pressure work, the analyst may
propose a temporary assumption, but it must be labelled, approved by the right owner, and paired with a trigger for
recalculation.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 8
1. Asking questions whose answers cannot change the work. | 2. Recording an answer without the owner who
approved it. | 3. Leaving 'TBD'
items with no deadline. | 4. Treating silence as approval.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
For each open item write: decision needed, impact if unresolved, owner, deadline, temporary assumption allowed?
yes/no. If still stuck: (1) restate the
decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the workbook; (4) save your genuine
attempt before opening review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Marketing and Finance disagree on whether refunded orders count in campaign revenue. Prepare
the agenda and decision log.
13. Validate your result
Every open question has an owner and a next action. Every resolved question is reflected in the scope or metric
contract.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain the difference between 'asking more questions' and 'reducing decision uncertainty'.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Attempt first. Then inspect the protected review and retry with a different stakeholder conflict.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Agenda + decision log + owner map + read-back summary + explain-back. RECOMMENDED VIDEO - requirements
interview 00:50-05:42: problem
definition through refinement. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=iIAbSOvf96E After saving evidence, continue to
SAF4.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 9
SAF4 - KPI ownership, metric contracts and definitions
1. Why it matters
Two teams can show different numbers while both calculations are arithmetically correct. The disagreement is often a
definition problem:
different populations, dates, exclusions, or sources.
2. What you are learning
Build a versioned metric contract for a KPI and distinguish label, business meaning, formula, eligible population,
exclusions, grain, time basis,
owner, source, target, and tolerance.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
SAF2 scope and SAF3 decision ownership.
4. Picture it in your head
Metric nutrition label: A KPI name is only the product name on the front. The contract is the label on the back:
formula, numerator, denominator, population, exclusions, time basis, grain, source, owner, version. Two teams
using different labels do not have the same metric.
5. New words before we use them
KPI: A metric tied to an important business objective or decision. Denominator: The population used underneath a
rate or percentage. Metric contract: A
documented agreement defining exactly how a metric is interpreted and calculated.
6. Watch / visual source
Versioned metric contract + one reconciliation rule + explain-back. RECOMMENDED REFERENCE - IIBA KPI
guidance Use for KPI framing; course contract
fields are authoritative for assessment.
https://www.iiba.org/professional-development/knowledge-centre/articles/kpis-for-business-analysts/
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report.
Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
source.
7. Follow with me once
- Net Revenue meaning: revenue recognized from completed order lines after approved returns and discounts.
- Formula: sum(line_amount - approved_return_amount - discount_amount). Grain: order line. Time basis: order
completion month.
- Return Rate meaning: returned completed order lines divided by eligible completed order lines. State whether partial
returns count by line or
- order.
- Name exclusions: cancelled orders, test orders, fraudulent orders if approved. Name owner: Finance for revenue
recognition; Operations may
- own operational return reason taxonomy.
- Add version date and tolerance: e.g. reconcile monthly Net Revenue to Finance control within 0.5% or investigate
before publishing.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A metric contract where another analyst could implement the same KPI without guessing hidden rules.
9. Why it worked
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 10
The metric is treated as a business agreement first and a formula second. Professional upgrade: Organizations often
separate metric owner, data owner, and
report owner. Do not assume the dashboard developer has authority to define the business metric.
10. Common beginner mistakes
1. Writing only the formula. | 2. Ignoring the denominator of a rate. | 3. Using dashboard label as definition. | 4.
Changing a metric silently when
the source changes.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
If two numbers disagree, compare contract fields one by one: meaning, population, exclusions, date basis, grain,
source, version. If still stuck: (1)
restate the decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the workbook; (4) save your
genuine attempt before opening
review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Define 'On-time Delivery Rate' for an executive dashboard. Include numerator, denominator,
exclusions, time basis, grain, owner,
source, target, and version.
13. Validate your result
Ask a second analyst to independently restate the numerator and denominator. If they cannot, the contract is not yet
clear.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why a KPI can be wrong even when the formula contains no error.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Attempt first, then compare against protected signals and retry with a different rate metric.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Versioned metric contract + one reconciliation rule + explain-back. RECOMMENDED REFERENCE - IIBA KPI
guidance Use for KPI framing; course
contract fields are authoritative for assessment.
https://www.iiba.org/professional-development/knowledge-centre/articles/kpis-for-business-analysts/
After saving evidence, continue to SAF5.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 11
SAF5 - Grain, lineage and source-of-truth decisions
1. Why it matters
Many believable BI errors come from combining tables that describe different things: one row per order, one row per
order line, one row per
return event, one row per monthly target. If the grain is not declared, joins can multiply values silently.
2. What you are learning
Declare grain and keys, map lineage from source to output, and choose the source-of-truth owner for each business
fact.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
Course 1 joins/model basics plus SAF4 metric contract.
4. Picture it in your head
One-row map: Put a sticky note above every table saying exactly what one row means. Draw arrows only after
that. Then mark one source as authoritative for each business fact. If two sources disagree, the map must show
who decides - not silently pick the easier number.
5. New words before we use them
Grain: What exactly one row represents. Lineage: The trace of where data came from and how it changed before
reaching the output. Source of truth: The
agreed authoritative system or owner for a particular business fact.
6. Watch / visual source
Source/grain register + lineage map + join-risk note + explain-back. RECOMMENDED CURRENT REFERENCE -
Power BI data lineage Use the lineage-view
idea as a visual analogy; no Power BI service access is required for this lesson.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-data-lineage
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report.
Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
source.
7. Follow with me once
- orders: one row per order. Key = order_id.
- order_lines: one row per order + line number. Key = order_id + line_id. Revenue is naturally calculated here.
- returns: one row per return event. One line can have multiple return events, so joining directly without aggregation
can duplicate line revenue.
- targets: one row per region-month. It is a higher-grain target and should not be joined blindly to each order line for
aggregation.
- Write lineage: source tables -> cleaning rules -> return aggregation -> metric calculation -> executive report. State
which system owns each
- fact.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A source/grain register plus a small lineage chain. Every table has a declared row meaning and key.
9. Why it worked
You prevented fan-out by deciding what each row means before joining or aggregating. Professional upgrade:
Source-of-truth is fact-specific. Finance can
own recognized revenue while CRM owns customer segment and Operations owns fulfillment status.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 12
10. Common beginner mistakes
1. Calling a file 'customer level' when it actually has multiple rows per customer. | 2. Choosing source of truth
because it is easiest to access. | 3.
Assuming a primary key without checking duplicates. | 4. Using DISTINCT to hide duplicated joins.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Before any join, write two sentences: 'One row in left table means...' and 'One row in right table means...'. Predict the
output grain before running the
join. If still stuck: (1) restate the decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the
workbook; (4) save your genuine
attempt before opening review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: You have ticket, ticket_event, agent, and monthly_team_target tables. Declare grain/key and draw
the lineage for 'resolved tickets per
team vs target'.
13. Validate your result
For every join, state expected row count direction and one duplicate/unmatched-key check.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain grain without using the word 'granularity'.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Save your source/grain register before opening the protected review. Fresh retry must use different table grains.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Source/grain register + lineage map + join-risk note + explain-back. RECOMMENDED CURRENT REFERENCE -
Power BI data lineage Use the
lineage-view idea as a visual analogy; no Power BI service access is required for this lesson.
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-bi/collaborate-share/service-data-lineage After saving evidence, continue to
SAF6.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 13
SAF6 - Assumptions, risks, limitations and analytical judgment
1. Why it matters
Decision-makers need to know not only what you found but how confident they should be. Mixing facts, assumptions,
and recommendations
makes a conclusion sound stronger than the evidence.
2. What you are learning
Label facts, assumptions, risks, limitations, and recommendations separately; calibrate recommendation strength to
evidence.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
SAF1-SAF5 decision, scope, metric, and source controls.
4. Picture it in your head
Four-box judgment board: Separate what you observed, what you assumed, what could go wrong, and what the
data cannot establish. Your recommendation is allowed to be only as strong as the weakest box that materially
affects the decision.
5. New words before we use them
Assumption: Something treated as true for the analysis but not fully proven. Risk: A possible future or hidden
condition that could make the result wrong or
harmful. Limitation: A known boundary of the data or method. Trigger: New evidence or a threshold that would
change the recommendation.
6. Watch / visual source
INTERNAL TEACHING ROUTE. No external video is required for this lesson. Use the mental model and worked
demonstration below as the canonical
teaching route.
7. Follow with me once
- Fact: East net revenue is 12% below the approved target for the current month after reconciliation.
- Assumption: the promotion calendar supplied by Marketing is complete.
- Limitation: offline store orders arrive one day later and are not yet included.
- Risk: if late offline orders are unusually high, the 12% gap may shrink materially.
- Recommendation: investigate the promotion mix before expanding discounts. Trigger: recompute after offline close;
reverse the
- recommendation if the gap falls below the agreed materiality threshold.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A decision note where evidence strength is obvious and the reader knows what could change the conclusion.
9. Why it worked
The recommendation is neither timid nor overconfident; it is tied to evidence and a change trigger. Professional
upgrade: Senior judgment often means
choosing the safest decision language: 'evidence supports', 'directional only', 'do not act until', or 'act now with
monitoring' based on consequence and
uncertainty.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 14
1. Calling an assumption a fact. | 2. Using 'probably' without naming the uncertainty. | 3. Listing limitations but
ignoring them in the
recommendation. | 4. Giving an irreversible action from weak evidence.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Highlight every sentence in your recommendation. Label it F/A/R/L/REC. Any sentence you cannot classify needs
rewriting. If still stuck: (1) restate the
decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the workbook; (4) save your genuine
attempt before opening review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Customer satisfaction fell after a support-tool migration, but survey response rate also changed.
Write
fact/assumption/risk/limitation/recommendation + trigger.
13. Validate your result
A reviewer should be able to identify exactly which new evidence could strengthen, weaken, or reverse the
recommendation.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why a limitation does not automatically make an analysis useless.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Attempt first. Retry on a scenario where the data limitation is different.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Calibrated decision note + trigger + explain-back. After saving evidence, continue to SAF7.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 15
SAF7 - Professional validation and reconciliation
1. Why it matters
A dashboard can look polished while containing a duplicated join, missing period, stale file, or wrong denominator.
Validation is not a final
glance; it is a planned second path that tries to prove the result wrong.
2. What you are learning
Design validation before delivery using row counts, coverage, duplicates, unmatched keys, control totals,
independent recomputation, business
invariants, tolerances, and recovery.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
Course 1 data-cleaning checks plus SAF4 metric contract and SAF5 grain.
4. Picture it in your head
Reconciliation triangle: Put source control, transformed data, and final output at three corners. Important
counts/amounts must travel around the triangle without an unexplained jump. If one edge fails, stop and repair
before presenting.
5. New words before we use them
Reconciliation: Comparing results against an independent control or alternate calculation. Tolerance: The maximum
acceptable difference before
investigation is required. Invariant: A rule expected to remain true if the data and logic are correct.
6. Watch / visual source
Validation log + independent control + failure-recovery note + explain-back. RECOMMENDED CURRENT
REFERENCE - Power BI data profiling Use the
profiling section as visual reinforcement for detecting unexpected/null values; course validation plan is b
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/clean-data-power-bi/
After watching/opening: return to this lesson and reproduce the worked example from your own file/query/report.
Save course-task evidence, not a screenshot of the
source.
7. Follow with me once
- Input check: confirm expected files and date coverage are present before calculating.
- Key check: detect duplicate order-line keys and unmatched return events.
- Control total: compare completed gross revenue to the operational source control.
- Independent recompute: calculate Net Revenue a second way using a separate grouped summary or pivot, not the
same formula copied twice.
- Business invariant: Net Revenue should not exceed eligible gross revenue. Record tolerance and recovery steps for
every failed check.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A validation plan with expected values or control methods, observed result, tolerance, status, and recovery path.
9. Why it worked
Different failure types have different checks; one green total cannot prove every part of the pipeline. Professional
upgrade: For important outputs, store
validation evidence with the release so future analysts can see what was checked, what tolerance was accepted, and
what failed.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 16
10. Common beginner mistakes
1. Validating with the same formula that produced the result. | 2. Ignoring a small mismatch without an agreed
tolerance. | 3. Fixing the data
silently instead of recording the cause. | 4. Treating 'no error message' as validation.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Ask: What wrong result could still look plausible? Design one check specifically to catch that failure. If still stuck: (1)
restate the decision; (2) fill only the
required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the workbook; (4) save your genuine attempt before opening
review.
12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Validate a support dashboard showing resolved ticket rate by team. Design at least six checks before
seeing the final dashboard.
13. Validate your result
At least one check must be independent of the main calculation and at least one must test grain/key integrity.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain the difference between checking that code runs and checking that a business result is trustworthy.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Attempt first. After review, design a changed validation plan for a different metric and source structure.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Validation log + independent control + failure-recovery note + explain-back. RECOMMENDED CURRENT
REFERENCE - Power BI data profiling Use
the profiling section as visual reinforcement for detecting unexpected/null values; course validation plan is b
https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/training/modules/clean-data-power-bi/ After saving evidence, continue to SAF8.
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 17
SAF8 - Documentation another analyst can inherit
1. Why it matters
If only you can refresh or explain the work, the team owns a fragile dependency. Senior-quality documentation lets
another analyst
reproduce the output and know when not to trust it.
2. What you are learning
Create an inheritable handoff pack covering purpose, definitions, sources/access, grain/keys, steps, validation,
limitations, refresh/run
instructions, owners, escalation, and change history.
3. Prerequisite / what you already know
SAF1-SAF7. You need one completed small analysis artifact to document.
4. Picture it in your head
Bus-factor test: Imagine you disappear for two weeks and a new analyst receives only your handoff. Can they
find the source, definitions, assumptions, refresh steps, validation evidence, known limitations, and next action
without messaging you? If not, the analysis is not inheritable.
5. New words before we use them
Runbook: Step-by-step instructions for operating or refreshing a repeatable process. Change log: A dated history of
material changes and why they were
made. Escalation owner: The person to contact when a rule, source, or process cannot be resolved by the analyst.
6. Watch / visual source
INTERNAL TEACHING ROUTE. No external video is required for this lesson. Use the mental model and worked
demonstration below as the canonical
teaching route.
7. Follow with me once
- Purpose: weekly executive check on net revenue, margin, and return rate; decision owner = Commercial Director.
- Definitions: link to metric-contract version and state effective date.
- Sources: exact source names, refresh timing, access owner, expected file/table grain.
- Run steps: numbered sequence from source refresh through transformation, validation, report refresh, and evidence
save.
- Checks and limitations: list required reconciliations, tolerances, known delayed source, and what to do if a control
fails.
- Ownership: report owner, metric owner, data owner, escalation path, and change history.
8. What you should see / be able to say
A new analyst can reproduce the normal run and recognize a failure without asking you what each step means.
9. Why it worked
The handoff documents decisions and failure handling, not just button clicks. Professional upgrade: Good
documentation is concise but executable. Keep
authoritative definitions in one controlled location and reference them instead of copying conflicting versions into
many files.
10. Common beginner mistakes
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 18
1. Writing 'refresh data' without naming the source or expected timing. | 2. Documenting only the happy path. | 3.
Leaving metric definitions inside
your head. | 4. Putting passwords or secrets into documentation.
11. If you get stuck - recovery ladder
Give the handoff to an imaginary analyst who has a clean folder and no chat history. Mark every sentence where they
would need to ask you a
question. If still stuck: (1) restate the decision; (2) fill only the required control fields; (3) use the partial template in the
workbook; (4) save your genuine

12. Now you do a small version alone
Fresh scenario: Document a monthly customer-retention report so a new analyst can run it next month. Include failure
and escalation paths.
13. Validate your result
Use the cold-handoff test: another person should identify inputs, outputs, definitions, steps, validations, limitations,
and owners from the document
alone.
14. Teach it back in your own words
Explain why documentation is part of analytical quality rather than administrative work.
15. Protected review + changed fresh retry
Attempt first, then compare against the protected review and rebuild one section from a changed failure scenario.
16. Evidence / mastery + exact next route
Handoff pack + cold-handoff checklist + explain-back. After saving evidence, complete the module mastery checklist
and follow the Gate A / completion
route.

masteryReview.text:
Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 1
C2_00 Module Test - Protected Review
RC4
Open only after a saved genuine attempt
Use each review to diagnose the missing reasoning, then close this file and solve the changed retry without
copying.
1. SAF1 - what strong reasoning contains
A strong answer names the decision/audience, metric definition, row grain/source, validation control, unresolved
risk/assumption, and handoff/acceptance rule before choosing stores. The important idea is not the exact wording; it
is refusing to start with ranking logic while the decision contract is undefined.
Changed retry: Operations asks which warehouse needs intervention; define release controls before ranking.
2. SAF2 - what strong reasoning contains
A defensible scope states who will act, what decision is possible, what "unhappy" means, eligible customer
population, period, row grain/source, segmentation, deliverable and acceptance. Open definitions remain explicit
instead of being silently invented.
Changed retry: Scope "marketing is inefficient" for a decision about next-month channel budget.
3. SAF3 - what strong reasoning contains
Questions should separate definition, owner/evidence, time/population and decision threshold. Example: Who owns
active-customer definition? What exact event makes a customer active? Which period/statuses are included? Which
decision changes if the definition changes?
Changed retry: Product and Support disagree about "resolved ticket"; write the clarification tree.
4. SAF4 - what strong reasoning contains
The two denominators create different populations, so the percentages answer different questions. A metric contract
should include name, purpose, numerator, denominator/population, exclusions, time basis, grain, source, owner,
version and acceptance/reconciliation rule.
Changed retry: Contract "on-time delivery rate" when teams disagree about promised vs revised ETA.
5. SAF5 - what strong reasoning contains
Orders are order-line grain; target is Region-Month grain. Aggregate actuals to Region-Month (or preserve separate
facts in a model) before comparing with targets. Never join target rows directly to order lines and then sum target
value.
Changed retry: Compare customer-month health with ticket-level support data without grain leakage.
6. SAF6 - what strong reasoning contains
Fact must be directly observed; assumption is an unverified explanation; risk is what could make the decision wrong;
limitation is what this evidence cannot establish. Recommendation should request/perform the next test rather than
claim the price change caused churn.
Changed retry: Revenue rose after a campaign; write a non-causal recommendation and change trigger.
7. SAF7 - what strong reasoning contains
Check duplicate/business keys, row counts, period coverage, population/denominator, source control totals, segment
reconciliation and invariants. Stop release, localize the first stage where reconciliation diverges, repair it, and rerun
downstream checks.
Changed retry: A dashboard count differs from source by 11 rows; define the reconciliation path.
8. SAF8 - what strong reasoning contains

Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 2
At minimum: decision/scope, definitions/metric contracts, source/grain/lineage, refresh steps,
transformations/calculations, validation evidence, assumptions/limitations, known issues, owner/access, output
location/version and next action.
Changed retry: Prepare an inheritable handoff for a monthly report owned by another team.
9. SYNTHESIS - what strong reasoning contains
Clarify decision -> contract metric/denominator -> state grain/source -> control duplicates -> compute only defensible
metrics -> validate independently -> separate fact/assumption/limitation -> compare decision rules/sensitivity ->
recommend with trigger -> handoff. An unresolved material denominator, grain, duplicate, validation or
evidence-strength issue blocks release.
Changed retry: "Which product should we discontinue?" with duplicate product IDs and an undefined
profitability denominator.

Page 1
HOW TO USE THIS REVIEW
Compare structure, not wording. Mark which competency failed, close the review, then solve the changed retry in the
workbook. Do not copy this review into your evidence. A reviewed answer is not a mastered answer.
STRONG C2-00 ARTIFACT
Decision explicit; scope bounded; metric contract versioned; grain and source-of-truth named; open questions have
owners; assumptions/risks/limitations separated; validation uses an independent control; recommendation strength
matches evidence; handoff is executable.
CRITICAL FAILURES
Silent definition invention; unresolved grain conflict; fabricated owner/evidence; missing independent reconciliation for a
material metric; recommendation stronger than evidence; opening protected material before saving the attempt.

2. Expected reasoning path
Decision contract
The stakeholder asks which city to fix first, but "first" could mean highest cancellation rate, highest actionable
cancellations, highest value at risk, or another operational rule. State the decision rule before ranking.
Data quality and denominator
There is one exact duplicate row. After removing/controlling it, 72 unique orders remain. Using all placed orders
produces a 66.7% cancellation tie between Bhubaneswar and Patna. Using accepted orders changes the rates to
64.7% and 68.8%, respectively.
Actionability sensitivity
Restaurant/driver cancellations are operationally different from customer cancellations. Bhubaneswar and Patna
each have six actionable cancellations in this fixture, so a simple actionable-count rule still ties them. Do not invent a
winner.
Recommendation boundary
A strong answer can recommend the next decision step (for example, confirm denominator/actionability and compare
operational capacity) without pretending the data supports a unique city priority when the selected rule does not
separate candidates.
Validation
Reconcile unique population, status counts, completed value (32,800.93 overall), segment totals and at least one
independent control. Explain how the duplicate and denominator choice affect the result.
3. Critical failure patterns
- Ranking cities before defining denominator/decision rule.
- Leaving the duplicate uncontrolled or using DISTINCT without documenting why.
- Treating customer and restaurant/driver cancellations as equally actionable without owner agreement.
- Claiming cancellation caused delay or campaign performance.
- Choosing Patna/Bhubaneswar as an automatic winner when the selected metric ties.

Course 2A | C2_00 | Astra Parity RC4
Page 3

Competency
Pass evidence
Decision/scope

Metric contract
Numerator, denominator, exclusions/actionability, time basis and owner/source are
explicit.
Grain/source
One row = order; duplicate controlled; source conflict documented.
Judgment
Fact vs assumption vs limitation separated; no causal overclaim.
Validation
Population/status/segment/control totals reconcile; sensitivity to denominator shown.
Handoff/defense
Another analyst can reproduce the decision and state what would change it.
PASS PHILOSOPHY: No percentage gaming. One unresolved material definition, grain, duplicate, validation, or
evidence-strength failure blocks the Gate even if other sections are polished.
5. Changed repair proof

dataset or instructor-assigned variant; define a new decision rule and show how alternate denominators could
change priority.

2. Expected reasoning path
Decision contract
The decision has two parts: identify where missed appointments occur and decide whether reminder policy should
change. Those are not the same claim.
Fixture diagnosis
After controlling one duplicate, 78 unique appointments remain. Central Clinic contains 26 no-shows; East Clinic
contains 26 cancellations; North Clinic contains 26 completions, including eight rescheduled flags.
Denominator logic
For a no-show rate, all appointments and "completed + no-show" are different eligible populations. State whether
cancellations belong in the denominator. East has no completed/no-show rows, so a completed+no-show
denominator is undefined there rather than zero.
Causal boundary
The extract does not prove reminder timing caused Central no-shows. Patient communications explicitly needs
evidence connecting reminder timing to the issue. Recommend a reminder-policy test only as a next experiment
unless additional evidence exists.
Validation
Reconcile clinic counts to 78 unique appointments; inspect rescheduled-ID semantics; compare no-show volume and
rate; test whether the ranking changes under approved denominator choices.
3. Critical failure patterns
- Calling East "best" on no-show rate while ignoring that its records are all cancellations.
- Dividing by a zero/undefined eligible population and reporting 0%.
- Treating rescheduled appointments as independent without resolving ID semantics.
- Claiming reminder timing caused no-shows from this extract.
- Changing policy without a decision threshold or test plan.
